atque instituti esset, cæteris omnibus ipse omissis, se Jesu Christi servum confessus est. Acriter 216 igitur percussus, custodiæ traditur, et magnas ibidem pertulit calamitates, jussis carceris custodibus non modo diligenter ipsum asservare; sed nemini permittere, ut ad illum curandum,seu ad aliqua ei afferendum esculenta introiret. Ergo post multos dies de carcere eductus, ac denuo coactus desciscere a Christo, idolisque sacrificare, et nullo modo ad id se induci passus, flagellis vehementer contunditur. Post hæc gladii subiens sententiam, capite plectitur.
Et certamen sacrosancti martyris Irenæi.
Exstitit hic, imperantibus Marco et Antonino, priscæ ætatis vir, apostolorum successor, episcopi munere in Lugduno civitate functus. Plures etiam conscripsit libros ad orthodoxam fidem confirmandam, a quibus ansa arrepta posteriores ad interpretandas divinas Scripturas, universo terrarum orbi eas exposuerunt. Celebris itaque virtute ac eruditione, postquam pro Christo certamen Pothinus episcopus consummavit, ipse præfatæ urbis episcopus designatur; ac multos infideles sermonibus, et doctrinis, adhortationibusque abstrahens, atque illos Christo martyres adjugens, tandem et ipse comprehensus a persecutoribus, et gladio confectus, ad Deum migravit, paratum sibi regnum recipiens.
EODEM MENSE. Die vicesima quarta 217 Certamen sancti martyris Tatiani.
Tatianus Christi martyr fuit ex Gratia regione: et apud Mantineum degens, atque ad se accedentes infideles fidem Christi edocens, ab ethnicis detentus, et catenis constrictus, Claudiopolim ducitur, ac traditur præfecto; veramque enuntians fidem crudeliter cæditur, et in carcerem mittitur. Postquam vero ærumnis fuit valde vexatus,iterum extractus, Christum cogitur denegare. Sed ad id nequaquam inductus, ingentibus fustibus percussus, et ignito ferro combustus; funibus postea vinctus, per mediam urbem raptatur, percussus et conculcatus. Cumque ad civitatis portam pervenisset, se crucis signo signans, audita desuper voce, quæ ipsi præparata dona annuntiabat, spiritum Deo tradidit: ejusque venerabiles reliquiæ in eadem civitate conditæ fuerunt.
Et certamen sancti martyris Eutychii discipuli sancti Joannis Theologi.
Eutychius Christi martyr Sehastopoli natus, propter Christi desiderium, patriæ, ac parentibus nuntio remisso, secessit ad Joannem Theologum, et illius evasit discipulus: cujus ipse virtutem imitatus, Dei gratia repletus fuit: divinoque zelo


[603] {#pg.117.603}
commotus, erroris munitiones evertit, idolorum fana solo æquavit, et infideles ad Christum convertens, baptizavit. Post Theologi autem transitum, discedens ad sanctum Paulum, passus est simul cum eo vincula, tormenta, atque flagella: et in fornacem etiam injectus, pluvia descendente, illamque exstinguente, exiit illæsus: ac belluis traditus vorandus, nullam ab eis læsionem accepit. Exinde a Dei angelo ductus, Ephesum proficiscitur; et sui magistri grege 218 reviso, iterum in propriam se contulit civitatem, ubi plenus dierum requievit.
Et memoria sancti Patris nostri Menæ archiepiscopi Constantinopolis.
Sanctus Pater noster Menas erat, Justiniano imperante, presbyter ecclesiæ Constantinopolitanæ. Propter ejus autem virtutem electus fuit Constantinopolis patriarcha, et a papa Romæ Agapeto consecratus, qui tunc temporis Roma illuc profectus ad componendas quæstiones ecclesiasticas, Anthimum hæreticum anathemate percellens, throno exturbaverat. Sed hoc Romam iterum reverso, et paulo post vita functo, alius Romanus pontifex fuit designatus, qui post aliquod tempus et ipse Constantinopolim petens, honoribus est affectus, atque amantissime exceptus tum ab imperatore, tum etiam a patriarcha; sed animi levitate elatus, pœnam sanctissimo Menæ irrogavit, ne amplius rem divinam faceret. Et iste quidem, utpote Dei pontifex, lætus pœnam subiit. At vero imperator ad iram commotus, injuriis affectum papam Romam remisit. Et post hæc sanctus Menas, probe grege directo, migravit ad Deum.
Et certamen beati martyris Georgii Limnœotæ.
Beatus Georgius primo ab adolescentia asceticum vitæ institutum in Olympi montibus agens, cum plura virtutis subiisset certamina; imperante postea Leone Isauro, qui sacras imagines aversabatur atque delebat, sanctorumque etiam reliquias incendio assumebat; divino ipse zelo impulsus, ante illum stans, et loquendi libertate arrepta, eum fortissime redarguit, atheum appellans, et Antichristi præcursorem imitatoremque. Comprehensus itaque, ac vehementer excruciatus, custodiæ fuit traditus, ex qua post multas ærumnas eductus, cogebatur chirographo cultum 219 venerabilium imaginum abnegare. Sed cum id facere nollet, diversa subiit tormentorum genera. Naribus deinde obtruncatis, atque capite exusto, gratias Deo agens, tradidit spiritum, annos natus quinque et nonaginta.
EODEM MENSE. Die vicesima quinta Memoria sancti apostoli Titi Cretæ episcopi.
Titus Christi apostolus prodiit ex insula Creta.


[604] {#pg.117.604}
χάριτος ἐπλήσθη θεοῦ. Καὶ θείῳ ζήλῳ κινηθείς, τὰ ὀχυρώματα τῆς πλάνης ἀνέτρεψε· τοὺς ναοὺς τῶν εἰδώλων κατέστρεψεν· τοὺς ἀπίστους ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον Χριστὸν ἐπιστρέφων ἐβάπτιζεν. Μετὰ δὲ τὴν μετάστασιν τοῦ θεολόγου, ἀπελθὼν πρὸς τὸν ἅγιον Παῦλον, συνεκακοπάθει αὐτῷ ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν, ὑπομένων δεσμὰ καὶ στρεβλώσεις καὶ μάστιγας. Ἐμβληθεὶς δὲ καὶ εἰς κάμινον, ἐξῆλθεν ἀβλαβής, ὑετοῦ κατελθόντος καὶ κατασβέσαντος αὐτήν. Καὶ θηρίοις δοθεὶς εἰς βρῶσιν, οὐκ ἠδικήθη παρ᾿ αὐτῶν· εἶτα ὑπὸ τοῦ θείου ἀγγέλου ὁδηγούμενος, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς Ἔφεσον, καὶ τὸ ποίμνιον τοῦ διδασκάλου ἐπισκεψάμενος, παρεγένετο πάλιν εἰς τὴν ἰδίαν πόλιν· ἔνθα πλήρης ἡμερῶν γενόμενος ἀνεπαύσατο.
Καὶ μνήμη τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Μηνᾶ ἀρχιεπισκόπου Κωνσταντινουπόλεως.
Ὁ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατὴρ ἡμῶν Μηνᾶς ὑπῆρχε μὲν ἐπὶ τῆς βασιλείας Ἰουστινιανοῦ πρεσβύτερος τῆς ἐν Κωνσταντινουπόλει Ἐκκλησίας, διὰ δὲ τὴν αὐτοῦ ἀρετὴν πατριάρχης προεχειρίσθη Κωνσταντινουπόλεως, χειροτονηθεὶς δὲ ὑπὸ Ἀγαπητοῦ πάπα Ῥώμης, ἀνελθόντος ἐκ τῆς Ῥώμης τότε, ἐπὶ διορθώσει τῶν ἐκκλησιαστικῶν ζητημάτων, καὶ ἀναθεματίσαντος Ἄνθιμον τὸν αἱρετικόν, καὶ τοῦ θρόνου ἀπελάσαντος. Ἀλλὰ τούτου πάλιν ὑποστρέψαντος εἰς Ῥώμην, καὶ μετὰ μικρὸν τελευτήσαντος, ἐχειροτονήθη ἕτερος. Καὶ μετὰ χρόνον τινὰ ἀνελθὼν καὶ αὐτὸς εἰς Κωνσταντινούπολιν, ἐτιμήθη, καὶ ἐλεξιώθη φιλοφρόνως παρὰ τε τοῦ βασιλέως, καὶ τοῦ πατριάρχου. Καὶ ὑπεραρθεὶς ὑπὸ κουφότητος, δέδωκεν ἐπιτίμιον τῷ ἁγιωτάτῳ Μηνᾷ μὴ λειτουργεῖν. Καὶ αὐτὸς μὲν ἐδέξατο χαίρων τὸ ἐπιτίμιον, ὡς θεοῦ ἀρχιερεύς. Ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς ὀργισθείς, μετὰ ὕβρεων ἀπεπέμψατο τὸν πάπαν εἰς Ῥώμην. Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ὁ ἅγιος Μηνᾶς καλῶς ἰθύνας τὸ ποίμνιον, πρὸς θεὸν ἐξεδήμησεν.
Καὶ ἄθλησις τοῦ ὁσιομάρτυρος Γεωργίου τοῦ Λιμναιώτου.
Γεώργιος ὁ μακάριος ἐκ νεαρᾶς τῆς ἡλικίας τὴν ἀσκητικὴν διαγωγὴν πρότερον ἐν τοῖς κατὰ τὸν Ὄλυμπον ὄρεσιν ἐκτελέσας, καὶ πολλοὺς ἀγῶνας ἐνδειξάμενος, ὕστερον ἐπὶ βασιλείας Λέοντος τοῦ Ἰσαύρου τοῦ τὰς ἁγίας εἰκόνας ἀποστρεφομένου καὶ ἀπαλείφοντος, καὶ τῶν ἁγίων λείψανα κατακαίοντος, ζήλῳ θεϊκῷ κινηθείς, καὶ σταθεὶς ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ, καὶ παρρησιασάμενος ἤλεγξεν αὐτὸν ἀνδρειότατα, ἄθεον εἰπὼν καὶ τοῦ Ἀντιχρίστου πρόδρομον καὶ μιμητήν. Κρατηθεὶς οὖν καὶ τιμωρηθεὶς ἰσχυρῶς παρεδόθη φυλακῇ· καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ ταλαιπωρηθεὶς ἱκανῶς, ἐκκληθεὶς αὐτῆς ἠναγκάζετο ἐγγράφως ἀρνήσασθαι τὴν τῶν σεπτῶν εἰκόνων προσκύνησιν. Μὴ πεισθεὶς δὲ πολυτρόποις βασάνων ἰδέαις προσομιλήσας, εἶτα τὴν ῥῖνα τμηθείς, καὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν καταφλεχθεὶς εὐχαριστῶν τῷ θεῷ τὸ πνεῦμα παρέδωκεν, ὑπάρχων ἐτῶν ἐνενηκονταπέντε.
ΜΗΝΙ ΤΩ ΑΥΤΩ. ΚΕ΄ Μνήμη τοῦ ἁγίου ἀποστόλου Τίτου ἐπισκόπου Κρήτης.
Τίτος ὁ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀπόστολος, ἐγένετο μὲν ἐκ


[605] {#pg.117.605}
τῆς Κρητῶν νήσου. Ἐν ἀρχῇ δὲ τοῦ βίου πολλὴν  ἐπιδειξάμενος σπουδὴν εἰς τὰ Ἑλληνικὰ μαθήματα, ἐκυμάζετο δὲ ἐπὶ σοφίᾳ παρὰ τῶν ἔξω· γεγονὼς δὲ ἐτῶν εἴκοσι, ἤκουσε φωνῆς λεγούσης αὐτῷ· Τίτε, δέον σε ἐντεῦθεν ὑποχωρῆσαι, καὶ τὴν ψυχήν σου σῶσαι· οὐ γὰρ ὠφελήσουσί σε τὰ μαθήματα ταῦτα. Ταύτης ἀκούσας τῆς φωνῆς, ἐσκέπτετο καθ’ ἑαυτόν, τί δεῖ ποιῆσαι. Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἀκούσας ὁ τῆς Κρήτης ἄρχων τοῦ Χριστοῦ θαύματα, προσεκαλέσατο αὐτὸν ὡς λόγιον, καὶ λέγει· Τίτε, θέλω ἀπελθεῖν σε εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ μαθεῖν, εἰ ταῦτα ἀληθῆ εἰσι, καὶ ἀναγγεῖλαί μοι. Ὁ δὲ ἀπελθών, τόν τε Χριστὸν εἶδε καὶ τὰ θαύματα, καὶ τοῖς πιστεύσασιν εἰς Χριστὸν συνηριθμήθη. Καὶ μετὰ τὸ πάθος καὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν, ἐπίσκοπος χειροτονηθεὶς ὑπὸ τῶν ἁγίων ἀποστόλων, ἀπεστάλη εἰς Κρήτην. Καὶ διδάξας  ἐν αὐτῇ τὸν λόγον τῆς ἀληθείας, ἐκοιμήθη ἐνενηκοντατεσσάρων ἐτῶν ὑπάρχων.
Καὶ μνήμη τῶν ἁγίων Πατέρων ἡμῶν Γενναδίου, Ἰωάννου, Στεφάνου, καὶ Μηνᾶ ἀρχιεπισκόπων γενομένων ἐν Κωνσταντινουπόλει.
ΜΗΝΙ ΤΩ ΑΥΤΩ. ΚΖ΄.
Ἄθλησις τῶν ἁγίων μαρτύρων Ἀδριανοῦ καὶ Ναταλίας.
Ἀδριανὸς ὁ τοῦ Χριστοῦ μάρτυς, καὶ Ναταλία ἡ χρηματίσασα σύμβιος αὐτοῦ, ὑπῆρχον μὲν ἐκ τῆς πόλεως Νικομηδείας. Ἰδὼν δὲ Ἀδριανός τινας Χριστιανοὺς κρατηθέντας ὑπὸ τῶν εἰδωλολατρῶν, καὶ βασανιζομένους, ἠρώτησεν αὐτούς· Διὰ τί ταῦτα ὑπομένετε; Καὶ ἀκούσας παρ’ αὐτῶν· Ὅτι διὰ τὰ ἀποκείμενα ἡμῖν ἀγαθὰ ἐκ Θεοῦ· κατανυγεὶς εὐθύς, καὶ παρεκάλεσεν τοὺς ἀπογραφομένους τῶν ἁγίων τὰ ὀνόματα, ἐντάξαι τὸ αὐτοῦ ὄνομα. Καὶ τούτου γενομένου, δραμοῦσα, ἡ Ναταλία ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ, κατησπάζετο τοῦ ἀνδρὸς τὰ δεσμά, προθυμοποιοῦσα αὐτὸν πρὸς τὸ μαρτύριον. Ὑποστρέψασα δὲ εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς, ηὔχετο ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ τελειῶσαι· τὸν δρόμον τῆς ἀθλήσεως. Ἐπεὶ δὲ παρέστησαν τῷ Μαξιμιανῷ, καὶ μεληδὸν κατεκόπησαν, παροῦσα ἡ Ναταλία συνέστειλεν αὐτῶν τὰ λείψανα. Καὶ ἀποκομίσασα εἰς τὸ Βοζάντιον, κατέθηκεν ἐν Ἀργυροπόλει. Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα καὶ αὐτὴ τελειωθεῖσα, ἐτάφη πλησίον αὐτῶν.
Καὶ ἄθλησις τοῦ ἁγίου ἑτέρου μάρτυρος Ἀδριανοῦ.
Ὁ τοῦ Χριστοῦ μάρτυς Ἀδριανὸς ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς βασιλείας Λικιννίου, υἱὸς μὲν ὑπάρχων Πρόδου τοῦ βασιλέως, καὶ ἀδελφὸς Δομετίου τοῦ γενομένου μετὰ Τῖτον ἐπισκόπου Βυζαντίου· πατὴρ δὲ Ὑρόβου καὶ Μητροφάνους, τῶν μετὰ ταῦτα γενομένων ἐπισκόπων. Τῆς οὖν τυραννίδος ἐπὶ Λικιννίου, καὶ Διοκλητιανοῦ κρατούσης, καὶ πολλῶν Χριστιανῶν καθ’ ἑκάστην φονευομένων, ὁ μακάριος Ἀδριανός, ἅμα μὲν ζηλῶν, ἅμα δὲ ποθῶν ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ μαρτυρῆσαι, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς Νικομήδειαν. Καὶ ἐμφανισθεὶς τῷ Λικιννίῳ, ὠνείδισεν αὐτῷ ὡς λυμαινομένῳ τὰ Ῥωμαϊκὰ στρατόπεδα, καὶ καταδαπα-


[606] {#pg.117.606}
AUGUSTUS.
Ab ineunte ætate plurimam ostendens in Græcorum disciplinis addiscendis sedulitatem, cum admiratione suspiciebatur ab ethnicis propter doctrinam. Ubi vero vicesimum ætatis annum attigit, audivit vocem sibi dicentem: Tite, hinc secedas, tuamque serves animam, oportet; non enim tibi proderunt hæ doctrinæ. Hac voce audita, secum ipse cogitabat, quid sibi esset agendum. Post hæc Cretæ præfectus auditis Christi miraculis, eum utpote sapientem accersivit, dicens: Tite, Hierosolyma te volo proficisci, et an vera hæc sint, intelligere, et mihi renuntiare. Hic igitur profectus, Christum vidit, ejusque miracula: ac sese eorum numero, qui in Christum crediderant, adjunxit. Post passionem autem et resurrectionem, episcopus a sanctis apostolis consecratus, in Cretam missus est; ubique cum veritatis verbum edocuisset, obdormivit, annos natus nonaginta quatuor.
Et memoria sanctorum Patrum nostrorum Gennadii, Joannis, Stephani, et Menæ archiepiscoporum Constantinopoleos.
EODEM MENSE. Die vicesima sexta
220 Certamen sanctorum martyrum Adriani et Nataliæ.
Adrianus Christi martyr, et Natalia ejus uxor, patriam habuere Nicomediam. Cum igitur Adrianus quosdam Christianos spectaret ab idololatris detentos atque excruciatos, interrogavit, cur hæc sustineret: ac audito ab illis, propter parati sibi a Deo bona cruciatus perferri, statim compunctus est; obsecrabatque eos, qui sanctorum nomina in tabulas referebant, ut suum etiam apponeret. Quo facto, occurrens ad carcerem Natalia, mariti vincula complectebatur ipsum excitans ad martyrium: dumque suam reversa, pro eo preces fundebat, ut certaminis cursum consummaret. Postquam autem martyres coram Maximiano steterunt, et fuere membratim obtruncati, astans Natalia, eorum collegit reliquias, ac transferens Byzantium, Argyropoli ipsas deposuit. Post hæc etiam ipsa finem accipiens, prope illos fuit sepulta.
Et certamen alterius sancti martyris Adriani.
Hic Christi martyr Adrianus exstitit temporibus Licinii imperatoris; filius quidem Probi imperatoris, frater autem Dometii illius, qui fuit post Titum Byzantii episcopus, pater vero Probi, et Metrophanis, qui postea episcopatum gesserunt. Itaque præpollente sub Licinio et Diocletiano tyranide, multisque ex Christianis in diem mactatis, beatus Adrianus zelo pariter atque martyrium pro Christo subeundi desiderio conflagrans, Nicomediam discessit; ac sese Licinio manifestans, exprobavit ei, quod Romanos perderet exercitus, et pecunias consumeret, bellumque non Barbaris,


[607] {#pg.117.607}
ἀντὶ τὰ χρήματα, καὶ μὴ πολεμοῦντι ἔθνη, ἀλλὰ Χριστιανούς. Κολακευθεὶς οὖν ὑπὸ τοῦ τυράννου, καὶ πιθανολογίαις ἀναγκασθεὶς ἀρνήσασθαι τὸν Χριστὸν, καὶ μὴ πεισθεὶς, φανερῶς ἐπεβουλεύθη, καὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀποτμηθεὶς, ἐτελειώθη. Τὸ δὲ λείψανον αὐτοῦ ἀνακομισθὲν ἐτέθη ἔνθα τὸ τοῦ ἁγίου Ἀδριανοῦ, καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν ἁγίων, καὶ Στάχυος τοῦ ἀποστόλου.
ΜΗΝΙ ΤΩ ΑΥΤΩ. ΚΖ´ Μνήμη τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Λιβερίου.
Λιβέριος ὁ μακάριος καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας ὑπέρμαχος ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς βασιλείας Κωνσταντίου ἐπίσκοπος Ῥώμης. Ὑπάρχων δὲ ζηλωτὴς τῆς ὀρθοδόξου πίστεως, ὑπεδέξατο τὸν μέγαν Ἀθανάσιον ὑποδιωχθέντα ὑπὸ τῶν αἱρετικῶν καὶ τοῦ θρόνου Ἀλεξανδρείας ἀπελαθέντα, παῤῥησιαζόμενος τὴν εὐσέβειαν. Ἕως γὰρ περιῆσαν Κωνσταντῖνος, καὶ Κώνστας οἱ πρῶτοι υἱοὶ τοῦ μεγάλου Κωνσταντίνου, ἐφυλάττετο ἡ ὀρθόδοξος πίστις· ἡνίκα δὲ ἐκεῖνοι ἐτελεύτησαν, καὶ κατελείφθη κύριος τῶν πραγμάτων Κωνστάντιος ὁ ἔσχατος υἱὸς, Ἀρειανὸς ὤν, ὑπερίσχυσαν οἱ αἱρετικοί. Ὅθεν καὶ Λιβέριος, μετὰ τὰ πολλὰ διαλεχθῆναι, καὶ ἐλέγξαι τὴν δυσσέβειαν τῶν αἱρετικῶν, ἐξωρίσθη εἰς Βέροιαν τῆς Θρᾴκης. Ἀλλὰ πίστιν καὶ ἀγάπην ἔχοντες οἱ Ῥωμαῖοι πρὸς αὐτὸν, προσῆλθον τῷ βασιλεῖ, ζητοῦντες αὐτόν. Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πάλιν ἀποσταλεὶς εἰς Ῥώμην, καὶ τὸ ποίμνιον αὐτοῦ καλῶς ποιμάνας ἐτελειώθη.
Καὶ μνήμη τοῦ ὁσίου Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ποιμένος τοῦ ἀναχωρητοῦ.
Ὁ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατὴρ ἡμῶν Ποιμὴν ὑπῆρχε μὲν ἐκ τῆς χώρας Αἰγύπτου· καταλιπὼν δὲ τὸν κόσμον, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ μοναστήριον, μετὰ τῶν γνησίων αὐτοῦ ἀδελφῶν, καὶ ἐγένετο μοναχός. Καὶ μετὰ χρόνους πολλοὺς ἀπελθοῦσα ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ ἰδεῖν αὐτοὺς, οὐκ ἠδυνήθη· ἀπέκλεισαν γὰρ αὐτῇ τὴν θύραν. Ὡς δὲ ἐπέμενε κλαίουσα, εἶπε πρὸς αὐτὴν ὁ Ποιμὴν, μὴ βλέπων αὐτήν· Τί θέλεις μῆτερ; Ἡ δὲ εἶπε, θέλω ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς. Καὶ λέγει ὁ Ποιμήν· Ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἐκείνῳ ὀψόμεθα ἀλλήλους. Ἡ δὲ ἀκούσασα ἀνεχώρησεν. Οὐ μόνον δὲ τοῦτο ἐποίησεν ἄξιον μνήμης, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἕτερα πολλά. Ὁ γὰρ ἄρχων τῆς χώρας κρατήσας τῆς ἀδελφῆς αὐτοῦ τὸν υἱὸν ἐπὶ κακίᾳ, ἐβούλετο τιμωρεῖν. Καὶ μαθὼν ὅτι τοῦ ἁγίου ἐστὶν ἀνεψιὸς, ἐμήνυσεν αὐτῷ, ὅτι: Εἰ ἄξιος, ἀπολύω αὐτόν. Ὁ δὲ ἀντεμήνυσεν· Ἐξέτασον τὰ κατ’ αὐτόν· καὶ εἰ ἄξιός ἐστι θανάτου, ἀποθανέτω· εἰ δὲ μὴ, ὡς βούλει ποίησον. Καὶ θαυμάσας ὁ ἄρχων τὸ ἀπροσπαθὲς αὐτοῦ, ἀπέλυσεν αὐτόν. Πολλὰ δὲ θαύματα ποιήσας, ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἀνεπαύσατο.
Καὶ μνήμη τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ὁσίου ἐπισκόπου Κορδούβης.
Ὁ Ὅσιος ἐπίσκοπος Κορδούβης, καταλιπὼν τὸν κόσμον, καὶ γεγονὼς μοναχὸς, καὶ ἐν ἀσκήσει πολλῇ πρότερον διαπρέψας, καὶ παντοίαις ἀρεταῖς διαλαμ-
sed Christianis inferret. Blanditiis igitur a tyranno A delinitus,atque persuasibilibus verbis coactus Christum abnegare, nec tamen ad id inductus, aperte impugnatur 221, et capite amputatus, martyrio fungitur. Ejus autem reliquiæ translatæ, eodem in loco fuere repositæ, ubi sancti Adriani, cæterorumque sanctorum, et Stachys apostoli reliquiæ jacent.
EODEM MENSE. Die vicesima septima Memoria sancti Patris nostri Liberii.
Beatus Liberius, veritatis propugnator,Constantio imperante erat Romæ episcopus. Cum vero zelo fidei orthodoxæ arderet, suscepit Athanasium ab hæreticis exagitatum, atque Alexandriæ throno expulsum, quod veritatem ipse clam defenderet. B Dum enim inter vivos agebant Constantinus et Constans majores natu filii Magni Constantini, orthodoxa fides servata est;sed ubi illi decesserunt, et relictus fuit rerum dominus Constantius minor natu filius,qui Arianus erat,prævaluerunthæretici. Quapropter etiam Liberius postquam multum redarguit, atque increpavit hæreticorum impietatem,in Berœam Thraciæ civitatem est relegatus. At cum Romani fide et dilectione erga illum essent devincti, accesserunt ad imperatorem, exposcentes eum : ac propterea Romam iterum missus, cum suum gregem recte gubernasset, decessit.
Et memoria sancti Patris nostri Pœmenis anachoretæ. C
Sanctus Pater noster Pœmen ex Ægypti fuit regione : derelicto autem mundo, secessit una cum suis germanis fratribus in monasterium, et monachus factus est. Multis post annis cum eorum mater ad eos invisendos profecta esset, id assequi minime potuit : occluserunt enim illi januam.Dum vero hæc in gemitibus persisteret, ait ad ipsam Pœmen, non intuitus eam. Quid optas, o mater? Hæc vero : Vos conspicere volo. Cui 222 Pœmen : In altero sæculo nos invicem videbimus. Quæ ut audivit, recessit. At non hoc solum memoria dignum iste gessit, sed et alia plura. Præfectus enim regionis, comprehenso sororis ejus filio propter admissum flagitium, decreverat supplicio in illum animadvertere : et cognito, quod sancti D nepos esset ex sorore, significavit ei, dicens: Si æquum censueris, dimittam eum. Cui Pœmen sic respondit : In illum diligenter inquire : et si mortis est reus, moriatur; si vero non, fac quod vis : Admiratus vero præfectus ejus animum affectibus nequaquam subjectum, illum dimisit.Plura autem sanctus operatus miracula, in pace quievit.

ψας, καὶ θαύμας: πολλοῖς κοσμηθείς, ἐχειροτονήθη παρὰ τοῦ τῆς Ῥώμης ἀρχιεπισκόπου τῆς πόλεως Κορδούης ἐπίσκοπος. Ζῆλον δὲ ἔχων ὑπὲρ τῆς ὀρθοδόξου πίστεως, παρεγένετο ἐν τῇ μεγάλῃ συνόδῳ τὴν τοῦ Ἀρείου μανίαν διελέγχων, καὶ τὴν ψυχοβλαβῆ αἵρεσιν ἀποκρουόμενος. Ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν γενομένην ἐν Σαρδικῇ σύνοδον αὐτὸς συνεκρότει, τὰ πρῶτα ἐν τοῖς τότε συνεληλύσουσιν ἐπισκόποις κεκτημένος. Ὕστερον δὲ ἐπὶ Κωνσταντίου τοῦ βασιλέως, Ἀρειανοῦ ὄντος, εἰς ἐξορίαν παρεπέμφθη, μετὰ καὶ ἄλλων πολλῶν ἐπισκόπων, τῆς ὀρθοδόξου πίστεως ἀντεχόμενος. Καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐξορίᾳ πολλὰ δεινὰ παθών, καὶ πλείστους πειρασμοὺς ὑπομείνας, πρὸς Θεὸν δι᾿ ὃν ἠγωνίσατο, χαίρων ἐξεδήμησεν.

Οὗτος ὁ μακάριος τῷ γένει ἦν Αἰθίοψ, τῇ δὲ χρόᾳ, μέλας ἀκριβῶς, οἰκέτης πολιτευομένου τινὸς, ὃν διὰ πολλὴν δυστροπίαν καὶ ληστρικὴν διαγωγὴν, ἀπώσατο ὁ ἴδιος δεσπότης. Οὗτος ποτε ποιμένι τινὶ ἐμνησικάκησε, παρεμποδίσαντι αὐτῷ εἰς πρᾶγμα, ὃν καὶ ἀποκτεῖναι ἐβουλεύσατο. Μαθὼν δὲ ὅτι πέραν τοῦ Νείλου ἐστί, πλημμυροῦντος τοῦ ὕδατος, τῷ στόματι δακὼν τὴν μάχαιραν, καὶ τὴν ἐπενδύτην τῇ κεφαλῇ ἐπιθεὶς, διανηξάμενος ἐπέρασε. Προαισθόμενος δὲ ὁ ποιμὴν τὴν αὐτοῦ ἔλευσιν, φυγὰς ᾤχετο. Ὁ δὲ, κριοὺς τέσσαρας ἐπιλέκτους σφαγήσας καὶ δήσας σειρᾷ, τὸν Νεῖλον ἀντεπέρασε κολυμβῶν. Τὰ κρέα δὲ φαγὼν καὶ τὰ κώδια οἴνῳ πλήσας, ἀπῆλθε πρὸς τοὺς ἑταίρους αὐτοῦ. Ταῦτα δὲ διηγησάμην ἵνα δείξω, ὅτ: δυνατόν ἐστι τοῖς βουλομένοις, διὰ μετανοίας σωθῆναι. Οὗτος ὀψέ ποτε κατανυγεὶς ἐκ τινος περιστάσεως, ἐπέδωκεν ἑαυτὸν μοναστηρίῳ. Καὶ οὕτως προσῆλθε τῇ μετανοίᾳ, ὡς καὶ τοὺς συμπράκτορας αὐτοῦ ἀγαγεῖν τῷ Χριστῷ. Καθεζομένου δέ ποτε ἐν τῷ κελλίῳ αὐτοῦ, λησταί τινες προσέβαλον αὐτῷ, ἀγνοήσαντες, εἶναι αὐτὸν τὸν Μωσῆν. Οὓς ὁ μακάριος δεσμήσας σχοινίῳ, καθάπερ σάκκον ἀχύρου, τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ ὤμοις ἐπιθεὶς, τῷ Κυριακῷ παρεγένετο, καί φησι πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφούς: Ἐπειδὴ οὐκ ἔξεστί μοι ἀδικεῖν, τούτους δὲ εὗρον ἐπελθόντας μοι, τί κελεύετε περὶ τούτων; Αὐτοὶ δὲ γνωρίσαντες αὐτὸν, ὅτι Μωσῆς ἐστιν ὁ περιβόητος λῃσταρχος καὶ ἀκαταγώνιστος, ἐξομολογησάμενοι τῷ Θεῷ καὶ αὐτοὶ, ἀπετάξαντο, καὶ γεγόνασι μοναχοί: δοκιμώτατοι. Θεαρέστως οὖν βιώσας ὁ ἅγιος γέρων, καὶ τὸν δαίμονα τῆς ἀκολασίας καταπαλαίσας, τελευτᾷ ἐτῶν ἑβδομήκοντα πέντε, γεγονὼς καὶ πρεσβύτερος, καὶ καταλιπὼν μαθητὰς ἑβδομήκοντα.

Ὅς ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν μαρτυρεῖται ὑπὲρ ἅπαντας εἶναι ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ, καὶ προφητῶν περισσότερος,

virtutibus, et miraculis exornatus, a Romano archiepiscopo episcopus urbis Cordubæ consecratur. Zelum autem habens pro fide orthodoxa, adfuit in magna synodo, Arii insaniam redarguens, atque hæresim animabus noxiam rejiciens. Sed et Sardicensem synodum ipse congregandam curavit, et primam sedem habuit inter episcopos, qui convenerant. Postea a Constantio imperatore Ariano in exsilium una cum aliis pluribus episcopis, qui orthodoxam fidem mordicus retinebant, pulsus, mulas in eo passus afflictationes, pluresque sustinens vexationes, lætus ad Deum, proquo decertaverat, migravit.
EODEM MENSE Die vicesima octava 223 Memoria sancti Patris nostri Moysis Æthiopis.
Beatus iste genere Æthiops, colore quam maxime niger, cujusdam civis servus, quem ipsius dominus expulerat propter ejus morum perversitatem, atque furandi consuetudinem. Hic cum in quemdam pastorem male animatus esset, quod ille sibi ad facinus patrandum fuerat impedimento, in animum sibi induxerat, eum de medio tollere. Certior autem factus ipsum trans Nilum agere, exundante aqua, ore gladium constringens, penula capiti superposita, nando transfretavit. At præsentiens pastor ejus adventum, fugiens abiit; ipse vero quatuor mactans eximios arietes, ac fune devinciens, natando Nilum iterum trajecit; et cum comedisset carnes; pellibus vino repletis ad suos socios rediit. Hæc enarravi ut ostendam, possibile esse volentibus per pœnitentiam consequi salutem. Iste vero tandem ex quodam casu compunctus, sese monasterio addixit: atque ita ad pœnitentiam accessit, ut suos etiam socios ad Christum adduceret. Aliquando ipso in cella sedente, quidam latrones impetum in eum fecerunt, ignorantes Moysen esse: quo beatus fune constringens, perinde ac paleæ saccum, suis imponens humeris, ad Basilicam se contulit; et fratribus ait: Quoniam mihi non licet ullam inferre injuriam, et hos reperi in me invadentes, quid de iis jubetis? Illi vero cognito, quod ipse Moyses esset, famosus ille latronum princeps, atque inexpugnabilis, Deo confessi, abdicato sæ- culo, monachi evaserunt probatissimi. Itaque sanctus senex vita Deo grata traducta, ac incontinentiæ dæmone devicto, moritur, annos natus quinque et septuaginta, presbyter etiam creatus, septuaginta discipulis post se relictis.

ὁ προσκιρτήσας ἀπὸ γαστρὸς, καὶ τοῖς, ἐν γῇ, καὶ ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ τὸν Χριστὸν κηρύξας, οὗτος ἦν υἱὸς Ζαχαρίου τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ Ἐλισάβετ, ἐξ ἐπαγγελίας Γαβριὴλ τεχθείς. Ἐτμήθη δὲ τὴν τιμίαν κεφαλὴν ὑπὸ Ἡρώδου διὰ τὴν παράνομον μῖξιν τῆς Ἡρωδιάδος. Οὗτος ὁ ἐξ αὐτῆς τῆς νηδύος ἁγιωσύνην περικείμενος, ἁγνείαν εἰσοικισάμενος, σωφροσύνην ἀσπασάμενος, ἀτροφίαν ἀσκήσας, καὶ πάσης ἀνθρώπων ἐπιμιξίας ἀπεῤῥωγώς, καὶ τὴν ἔρημον ὡς πόλιν οἰκήσας, θηρίοις συνδιαιτώμενος, καμήλου θριξὶ σκεπόμενος, δερματίνῃ ζώνῃ περισφιγγόμενος, καὶ ἴσα πτηνῷ τὸ τῆς τροφῆς κεκτημένος αὐτόματον, μελέτην δὲ διηνεκῆ, τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ νόμον ποιούμενος, ἡγεῖτο τῆς αὐτοῦ φυλακῆς καὶ τηρήσεως, πάντα δεύτερα καὶ ὑποδεῆ, ὁ τοὺς ὅρους ὑπερβὰς τῆς φύσεως, καὶ τὸν καθαρὸν καὶ ἀμόλυντον καὶ πάσης ἐπέκεινα φύσεως βαπτίσας Χριστόν. Τοίνυν ὁ πολλήσας ἐν ἀκολασίᾳ Ἡρώδης, τοῦ Ἰουδαϊκοῦ τετραρχῶν ἐδάφους, τὴν τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ Φιλίππου γυναῖκα πρὸς γάμον ἠγάγετο. Θείῳ οὖν κινηθεὶς ζήλῳ ὁ προφήτης, καὶ ἀληθείας ὅπλοις φραξάμενος, ἔλεγε πρὸς τὸν τύραννον· Οὐκ ἔξεστί σοι ἔχειν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου. Ἐντεῦθεν φυλακὴ καὶ δεσμὰ περὶ τὸν ἅγιον, τοῦ μανικοῦ γυναίου πρὸς τοῦτο τὸν ἐραστὴν συνελάσαντος. Ὅθεν γενεθλίων τελουμένων, καὶ πότου δαψιλοῦς καὶ φιληδόνου πρὸς παραφροσύνην ἐκκυλίσαντος τὸν ἑστιάτορα, ὄρχησις ἑταιρικοῦ θυγατρίου, καὶ μισθός, προφήτου ἀναίρεσις. Αὐτίκα οὖν ἤχθη ἐπὶ πίνακος ἡ τοῦ δικαίου κεφαλή, ἐπεδέθη μάχλῃ καὶ μοιχαλίδι γυναικί, ἔτι τὸ αἷμα στάζουσα, καὶ τὰ αὐτὰ φθεγγομένη. Ἐτελεῖτο δὲ ταῦτα ἐν τῇ Σεβαστῇ πόλει ἀπεχούσῃ τῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἡμέρας ὁδὸν, ἔνθα καὶ ὁ μετ᾿ ἐκεῖνον ἄρξας τετράρχης, τοὺς ἀνακτορικοὺς ἐπήξατο δόμους. Καὶ ὁ προφητοκτόνος ἐτελέσθη πότος, ἐκεῖ καὶ τὸ προφητικὸν ἐκεῖνο καὶ ἅγιον περισταλὲν παρὰ τῶν ἰδίων μαθητῶν ἀπεκρύπτετο σῶμα.

Ἐν τούτοις ἑξήκοντα χρόνοις διαρκέσας, Βιτάλιον καὶ Νικηφόρον τοὺς αὐτοῦ παραλαβὼν μαθητὰς, τῇ Πελοποννήσῳ προσεπιβαίνει. Venerandum autem ei caput ab Herode obtruncatur propter scelestum regum cum Herodiade concubitum. Ab ipso matris sinu sanctitatem iste indutus, puritatem suscipiens, temperantiam amplexus, in cibi abstinentia se exercens, ab omni hominum conversatione remotus, eremum, ut urbem, habitavit, cum belluis vivens, cameli pilis vestitus, ac zona ex corio præcinctus ; et instar volucrum, cibo utebatur a natura sponte oblato : assidue legem Dei meditabatur, cujus observantia, atque custodia nil ipsi unquam antiquius. Hic ipsos naturæ terminos transcendit ; et purum atque immaculatum super omnem naturam Christum baptizavit. B Cum itaque Herodes libidini valde indulgens, Judaicæ regionis tetrarcha, fratris sui Philippi uxorem sibi in thalami consortium duxisset, divino excitatus zelo propheta, et veritatis armis munitus, ait ad tyrannum : Non licet tibi habere uxorem Philippi fratris tui. Hinc carceres et vincula in sanctum, furibunda femina in id amatorem impellente. Quapropter dum natatalia celebrarentur convivia, opiparis, atque voluptariis compotationibus ad mentis impotentiam convivatore devolventibus, en chorea meretriciæ puellæ, et præmium cædes prophetæ. E vestigio igitur allatum super disco justi caput et lascivienti, atque adulteræ feminæ traditum, adhuc sanguinem stillans, eamdemque proferens vocem. Ὁ τοῦ μεγάλου Θεοδοσίου υἱὸς ᾿Αρκάδιος, τὴν τιμίαν ζώνην τῆς ὑπεραγίας Θεοτόκου ἐξ Ἱεροσόλυμων ἐξαγαγών, φυλαττομένην ἐκεῖσε μέχρι τοῦ τότε καιροῦ μετὰ καὶ τῆς τιμίας ἐσθῆτος, ὑπὸ παρθένου γυναικός τινος · καὶ ἐν Κωνσταντινουπόλει ἀποκομίσας, κατέθετο ἐν λαμπρᾷ θήκῃ, ἣν καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ἁγίαν σορόν. Χρόνων δὲ διεληλόντων τετρακοσίων δέκα, Λέων ὁ βασιλεὺς ἤνοιξε τὴν ἁγίαν  ταύτην σορόν, διὰ τὴν τοῦτο σύζυγον Ζωὴν ἐνοχλουμένην ὑπὸ πνεύματος ἀκαθάρτου, ἥτις καὶ ἠξιώθη θείας ὀπτασίας· ὡς εἰ ἐπιτεθῇ ἡ τιμία ζώνη ἐπ᾿ αὐτῇ, τεύξεται τῆς ἰάσεως. Εὑρέθη οὖν ἡ τιμία ζώνη, ὡς νεοφαντος, ἀποστίλβουσα, σφραγῖδα ἔχουσα διὰ χρυσίνης βούλλης, καὶ κωδικελλων ἐμφαίνοντα λεπτομερῶς, καὶ τόν τε χρόνον, τὴν Ἰνδικτιῶνα, καὶ τὴν ἡμέραν, καθ᾿ ἣν ἐν Κωνσταντινουπόλει προσεκομίσθη ἡ ἁγία ζώνη· καὶ πῶς ἐτέθη χερσὶ τοῦ βασιλέως ἔνδον τῆς θήκης ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ σφραγισθεῖσα. Ἦν καὶ ἀσπασάμενος ὁ βασιλεύς, καὶ διὰ χειρὸς τοῦ τηνικαῦτα πατριάρχου ἄνωθεν τῆς βασιλίσσης ὑφαπλωθεῖσα, ἐλευθερίαν τοῦ νοσήματος εἰργάσατο. Καὶ πάντες τὸν Σωτῆρα Χριστὸν δοξάντες, καὶ τῇ πανάγνῳ αὐτοῦ Μητέρι ὕμνους εὐχαριστηρίους  ἀποδόντες, κατέθεντο τὴν ἁγίαν ζώνην ἐν τῇ τιμίᾳ σορῷ, ᾗ προϋπῆρχεν.

EODEM MENSE. Die tricesima prima Depositio venerandæ zonæ sanctissimæ Deiparæ.
Arcadius Magni Theodosii filius venerandam sanctissimam Genitricis Dei zonam Hierosolymis educens, ubi usque ad illa tempora una cum pretiosa veste fuerat a quadam virgine asservata, eamque Constantinopolim transferens, deposuit in eleganti theca, quæ sancta urna fuit appellata. Quadringentis post annis Leo imperator hanc sanctam urnam aperuit propter uxorem ipsius Zoen ab impuro spiritu vexatam, quæ divina visione digna habita fuerat, atque admonita, fore ut, si ei veneranda zona imponeretur, incolumitatem obtineret. Itaque reperta fuit adoranda zona, perinde ac recens contexta, refulgens, aurea signata bulla, et codicillo adamussim 226 indicante annum, indictionem et diem qua Constantinopolim fuerat sacra asportata, utque imperatoris manibus intra thecam deposita, et ab ipso signata. Eam amplexus est imperator; et per manum tunc temporis patriarchæ super imperatricem explicata, a morbo liberam illam effecit. Cunctis demum Salvatorem Christum glorificantibus, atque immaculatissimæ ejus matri hymnos pro gratiarum actione reddentibus, reposita fuit sancta zona in veneranda urna, in qua antea exstabat.
I. De struendis ecclesiis, et religiosis domibus. Argumentum. Ex Balsamone Antiocheno patriarcha. — Basilius junior Nicephori Phocæ legem, qua ille statuerat, ne novo monasteria, vel xenones, vel gerocomia conderentur, per novellam hanc abolet; quæ fuit edicta mense Aprili, indictione prima, anno mundi ςχς΄.
Divinitus constituta majestas nostra, cum et a monachis, quorum testata pietas atque virtus
incited the saint, through the night, with voices and clamors to attack him. But when they achieved nothing, they departed defeated. He, however, having constructed a narrow cell for himself, and having entered into it, passed the whole time of his life there.
Eodem die
Commemoration of the holy women Marana and Cyra. A These holy women were from the city of Beroea in Cilicia. Having left behind both family and fatherland, and wealth, they went near to Beroea and built a small cell; and having entered within, they blocked up the door with clay and stones. And they left a small window, from which they would receive a little food and a small amount of water. And they would converse with the women who came to them, teaching them virtue. They also weighed down their whole bodies with great weights of iron; and they spoke with women only on the day of Pentecost, passing the whole remainder of the year in silence. They ate and drank only once in forty days. And since they lived in this manner piously and religiously, they were also deemed worthy of the gift of miracles; for they restored sight to the blind, healed the demon-possessed, and granted the power of walking to the lame; and thus they passed away.
Eodem die
Commemoration of Saint Domnina.
Saint Domnina was born in the city of Cyrrhus to pious and wealthy parents; burning from youth with the love of God, she devoted herself entirely to religious exercises: and in a hut which she had built from reeds contiguous to her house, she shut herself in: where, throughout the day and night, she prayed to God for the whole world, for the churches, for the orthodox emperors, for the army, for the state, and finally she made her own last prayer for her own soul. And her food was boiled lentils and a little water. Having thus lived like the angels, with her body worn down by labors, she migrated with joy to God, whom she had loved, receiving the enjoyment of eternal goods.
MENOLOGION OF THE GREEKS
PART THREE
FROM THE MONTH OF MARCH TO AUGUST.
MONTH OF MARCH.
The first day.
1 The contest of the holy martyr Eudocia the Samaritan.
Saint Eudocia, martyr of Christ, [was] from the city of Sa-
Samaria. During the reign of Trajan, she first lived a licentious life, and having many lovers on account of the beauty of her face, she gathered immense wealth from them. But later, having been taught the word of repentance by a certain monk named Germanus, she was struck with compunction. Then, also impelled by a vision, she approached Theodotus the bishop and was baptized by him. The vision was of this kind: she saw an angel of God leading her by the hand to heaven, and other angels rejoicing; but at the same time a certain black, raging one, saying that a great injustice had been done to him, because Eudocia had become a Christian. For this reason, she distributed her wealth to the poor and became a nun. And having been denounced by her own lovers, she stood before the Emperor Aurelian and was punished. But after she had raised his own son, who had died, to life through prayer, she persuaded him to believe in Christ. And then she was released, but later, being seized by the governor of the region, she was beheaded.
The contest of the holy martyrs Nestor and Tribimaeus.
During the reign of Decius the ungodly, these holy martyrs Nestor and Tribimaeus were at the city of Perge, in the region of the Cibyrraeotes. Because they were Christians and preached Christ with freedom and boldness, they were denounced to the governor of the region. He immediately sent a multitude of soldiers, had them brought in bonds, and presented them before his tribunal, having set out before them all the instruments of torture. But seeing that they despised his threats and confessed Christ with a loud voice, he ordered them to be stripped and cruelly beaten with dried bull-sinews, and then hung up and lacerated until their entrails appeared. But seeing them have an unchangeable mind toward our Lord Jesus Christ, he had them taken down from the wood and delivered them to the executioners, by whom their venerable heads were cut off with swords; and thus, having been perfected with thanksgiving, the Lord received them.
ON THE SAME MONTH. The second day.
The contest of the holy martyr Antonina.
Antonina, the martyr of Christ, was from the city of Nicaea, under the reign of Maximian. Being a Christian, she manifested herself to the same Maximian when he had come to Nicaea; and being brought into his presence, she confessed Christ with boldness. For this reason, she was tortured, in order that she might be compelled to deny Christ and sacrifice to the idols. But as she was not persuaded, she was thrown into prison. Then, being brought out of prison and again compelled to deny Christ, when she would in no way agree, she was ordered to be suspended on high and torn at the sides. But when Maximian saw her mocking his error and proclaiming the truth, he ordered the executioners to strip her and
to carry her off, angels came who protected her but punished them. Then she was placed upon a red-hot gridiron, yet she remained unharmed. Afterward, having been placed in a sack, she was cast into the marsh of Nicaea, and so she finished her martyrdom.
On the same day.
The Dormition of the apostle Parmenas.
This holy apostle Parmenas, being a disciple of the holy apostles, was numbered among the Seventy. He was chosen and appointed with the other six deacons to minister to the tables of those who were coming to Christ and being baptized, just as the holy Luke writes in the Acts of the Apostles, saying: "And they chose" (namely, the holy apostles) "Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Nicolaus a proselyte of Antioch, and Parmenas." Thus, therefore, did Parmenas minister, and by faithfully and devoutly applying his toil to the needs of the saints, and pleasing God and His disciples and apostles, he was seized by a disease; and having finished his life before the eyes of the apostles, he departed to Christ, whom he had desired, having obtained an unfading crown and an immortal kingdom.
And the contest of Saint Quintus the Wonderworker: and the dormition of the saints Andronicus and Athanasia: also the memory of Saint Troadius, and of the holy hieromartyr Porphyrius of Gaza, and of Theodoret the presbyter of Antioch: and finally the contest of the holy hieromartyr Theodotus, bishop of Cyrenia.
IN THE SAME MONTH.
The Third Day.
 The contest of the holy martyrs Eutropius, Cleonicus, and Basiliscus.
These men lived in the times of Maximian, serving as fellow soldiers and kinsmen of Saint Theodore. Being brought before the governor as Christians, they were received with dire scourging, to such an extent that the torturers themselves grew weary from the intensity of the torments. But the martyrs, when the Lord appeared to them along with the holy great martyr Theodore, were made whole. Whereupon the governor, changing his strategy, attempted with blandishments to turn Saint Cleonicus away from the faith of Christ, promising him gifts and honors. But he, smiling, exposed the impotence of the idols to ridicule. For when a sacrifice was being made to them, he cast down the image of Artemis with his prayers. Wherefore they poured pitch and bitumen, boiled in three cauldrons, upon the holy martyrs: yet they were preserved safe and unharmed; but the torturers were consumed by fire. Then Cleonicus and Eutropius were fastened to crosses and finished their martyrdom; but Basiliscus was cast into prison, and after some time he too passed from this life.
IN THE SAME MONTH. Fourth Day.
Memory of our holy Father Gerasimus.
Gerasimus the wonderworker abandoned the world and became a monk. Retiring to the inner desert of the Thebaid region, he lived in quiet, fulfilling the commandments of God. He attained such intimacy with God that, representing in himself the image and likeness of the saints, he both commanded wild beasts and performed many miracles. He also had an ass to transport water, as the water was far away. But a lion having come down from the mountain to him to seek a cure for its eye, which had been struck by a thorn, he cured it; and after it was healed, he commanded it to lead the ass to pasture and graze it. The lion would therefore lead it by a halter and graze it. And once, while the lion was sleeping, passing merchants took the ass away. Gerasimus, suspecting that the lion had eaten it, condemned it to carry water in the ass's stead, which it continued to do until the elder’s death. Upon his death, it also fell dead upon his grave.
And memory of our holy Father Marcus.
Saint Marcus was a lover of labor in all things, and gave himself up to the meditation of the divine Scriptures, thereby arriving at the highest pinnacle of virtue. Clear signs of this are both the books full of utility written by him concerning virtue, and the grace of the miracles performed by him. For while he was living a quiet life in seclusion, a hyena approached him, bearing her own blind cub, and with a humble gesture begged him to have mercy on the blindness of her offspring. Observing this, he spat into its eyes and made them whole. After some days, the hyena returned and brought to the saint the skin of a large ram as a reward for the cure. He would not accept it before the beast promised no longer to harm the sheep of the poor. If he showed such affection toward irrational animals, what must we think he felt toward humans? Such, moreover, was his purity that the presbyter of the place would affirm that he never gave communion to Marcus, but that it was extended to him by the hand of an angel. Having reached his hundredth year, he was perfected.
And the contest of the holy martyrs Paul and his sister Juliana, and Stratonicus in the city of Ptolemais.
IN THE SAME MONTH. Fifth Day.
Contest of the holy martyr Eulogius.
Eulogius, the martyr of Christ, was from the region of Palestine, the son of wealthy, but idolatrous parents. He, however, having embraced the faith of Christ and been baptized, after the death of his parents distributed the vast riches left to him among the poor, and willingly living by begging for the Lord's sake, he went about every city and region...
teaching the word of Christ, converting many from among them, and baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. While doing this, he was denounced by the idolaters to the prince of the region. Being arrested, he was brought before him; and upon being questioned, he freely confessed Christ. Wherefore, being stripped of his garments and cruelly beaten with dry ox-hide thongs, and compelled to deny Christ and sacrifice to the idols, because he would not comply, by the prince’s order his sacred head was cut off, and he was buried in the same place.
And the memorial of our holy Father Gregory, bishop of Constantia in Cyprus; and likewise the memorial of Hesychius the ascetic.
ON THE SAME MONTH.
The sixth day.
The Contest of the holy martyr Conon in Isauria
This holy Conon, in the times of the holy apostles, was a native of the region of Isauria. But although he was a Christian, he persuaded the woman whom he had married, before they came together, that they both should preserve their virginity; wherefore he lived with her just as a sister. Furthermore, he had as a leader of his salvation the archistrategos Michael, who both baptized him, and taught him the name of the Holy Trinity, and imparted the divine mysteries to him, and was with him even to the end; moreover, he conferred upon him the power of performing marvelous miracles. Conon therefore baptized his own parents, of whom Nestor his father underwent martyrdom for Christ. But he also convinced his adversaries, Greeks who affirmed that there was no God besides idols, and persuaded them to confess Christ with a loud voice and to say: "One is the God of Conon." He also subdued the demons; and some of them were assigned by him to wilderness places, while others were shut up in jars. Finally, being arrested by the governor and subjected to torture, but rescued by the people, who ran to his aid, he lived for two years thereafter and ended his life.
And the contest of the holy martyr Conon the gardener
This man was a native of Nazareth in Galilee during the reign of Decius. Having gone into the region of Pamphylia, and taking possession of a small piece of land, he converted it into a garden, and from the vegetables planted there he prepared sustenance for himself and for his poor guests. He was so simple in his ways that when those came who were to arrest him and bring him before the governor to be subjected to tortures because he was a Christian, and when they greeted him in mockery, he returned the greeting; and when they said that the governor sent for him, he replied: "What need does he have of my work, especially since I am a Christian?" Being bound, however, and brought to the governor, and when he was compelled to sacrifice to the idols, he sighed deeply and said to the governor: "Would that you, O governor, would also deny the idols and come to Christ." Therefore, having his ankles pierced and being fixed with iron nails, and compelled to run before a chariot, he ended his life.
The contest of the forty-two holy martyrs captured at Amorium and slain in Syria.
In the reign of Theophilus the Iconoclast, the father of Michael, the son of Theodora who restored Orthodoxy, these saints were commanders and tribunes, men of wealth and noble birth. At that time, the emir came from Syria with an innumerable host against the eastern parts of the Roman Empire, and they were sent by the emperor to guard the city of Amorium. Seeing the infinite multitude of the Saracens, they entered within the fortress and defended it courageously. But with the permission of God, who chastens those who err, the fortress was taken by force and the multitude of the citizens was slaughtered. They themselves were taken prisoner, led away into Syria, and shut up in prison. And after enduring many hardships, they were brought out of the prison and compelled by force to embrace their [the Saracens'] illusions. But steadfastly refusing this, they received the sentence of death by beheading. And when Constantine had greatly encouraged his companions, he was beheaded with them.
ON THE SAME MONTH. The seventh day. Saint Paul the Confessor of Prusia.
When this man was bishop of the holy Church in Prusia during the times of the impious Iconoclasts, and saw those madmen raging against the Churches of Christ and overturning all precision of the laws, and destroying the forms and representations of the venerable icons—wholly exterminating them from the inner sanctuaries of the holy temples and substituting in their place painted figures of wild beasts, birds, and snakes, while disregarding the traditions of the divine Fathers—as a victor for God, he did not cease to attack them with divine words like arrows, gladly enduring persecutions, exiles, and most grievous hardships for the sake of the holy icons of Christ our God, and of His most holy and spotless Mother, our glorious Lady, the Theotokos and ever-virgin Mary, and of the God-like angels, and of all the saints. Therefore, having endured much vexation over the course of many years, and having struggled nobly to his final breath, he migrated to the Lord.
And the memory of the holy Arcadius and Nestor, bishops of Trimithous in Cyprus; and the contest of the holy Eubulus and Julian the physician, and of the venerable Dometius; and of the seven holy martyrs in Cherson.
ON THE SAME MONTH. The eighth day. Memory of the holy confessor Theophylactus, Bishop of Nicomedia.
Theophylactus, the divine high priest, was born in the eastern parts. Coming to Constantinople, he served the most holy Tarasios while the latter was still the first of...
the secretarial order. When he became patriarch, he made him a monk, together with Michael, who was afterwards created bishop of Synada, and he enrolled them in the oratories of the Patriarchate. Afterwards, he ordained him bishop of Nicomedia. When Tarasios ceased to be among the living, and Saint Nicephorus succeeded him in the patriarchate, as Leo the Armenian assumed the empire and arrayed himself against the holy images, Saint Nicephorus, summoning Saint Theophylactus along with the other bishops, entered the palace and harshly rebuked the impious emperor who was opposed to the holy images. Then the patriarch was banished to the island of Thasos; others were deported to other places, but Theophylactus to Strobilos, where he ended his life.
Et memoria sancti Arcadii Cyprii, ac certamen Eubuli et Juliani. [And the memory of the holy Arcadius of Cyprus, and the contest of Eubulus and Julian.]
Saint Arcadius was a native of the island of Cyprus, having embraced the monastic life from childhood, and on account of his upright way of living, he was most pleasing to God, beginning the arena of his struggle during the reign of Constantine the Great. He profited many, not only by the example of his life and his virtues, but also by his teaching and exhortations. Among these were Eubulus and Julian, who came to him more frequently, and being comforted by his sermons, they proceeded on the path of virtue. Afterwards, however, under the reign of the impious Apostate Julian, they were captured by the idolaters who had received power from the emperor to rise up freely against the Christians; and at length, after the harshest tortures, they were beheaded. When Saint Arcadius learned of these things, he was indeed saddened; yet he gave thanks to God, who had ordained all things in this way. Persevering, however, in the same place where he had hitherto resided, he ended his life, steeped in many tears during his prayers.
Et certamen sanctorum in Chersone episcoporum Basilei, Eugenii, Agathodori, et reliquorum. [And the contest of the holy bishops in Cherson: Basil, Eugenius, Agathodorus, and the rest.]
During the reign of Diocletian, Hermon, bishop of Jerusalem, commissioned bishops, sending Ephrem to Turkey and Basil to Cherson. When the latter preached Christ there, he was met with scourging and driven out of the city. But when he had called the son of the ruler back from death to life, he was summoned back, and he baptized the ruler himself and many others. But those who had remained in their infidelity dragged him, tied by his feet with ropes, for so long that he ended his life. After his death came Eugenius, Agathodorus, Capeton, and Elpidius, who, while they were preaching Christ, were killed by the Greeks who were rising up against them. After these things, Aetherius was sent from Jerusalem, and when he saw the ferocity of the people, he approached the Great Constantine, then reigning in Byzantium, and asked that the idolaters be cast out of the city of Cherson; this happened according to his desire. And when he had built churches and had approached the emperor again to give thanks, and had returned to Cherson—bringing sacred things with him—on his way back he was cast into the river Dnieper and ended his life there.
MONTH OF THE SAME. Day Nine.
Certamen (Contest) of the holy martyrs of Sebaste.
The forty martyrs of Christ, hailing from various places, were serving in the army during the reign of Licinius. Because they were Christians, they were seized by the governor Agricolaus, in the presence also of the duke, and were compelled to sacrifice to idols. As they would not be persuaded, their mouths were struck with stones. Then, in the winter season, they were ordered to pass the night naked upon the lake, which was frozen over by the cold and had turned to ice. There, when one man, whose spirit had failed him in bearing the cold, leaped into a nearby bath and was killed by the heat, the jailer who guarded them, seeing crowns descending from heaven upon the thirty-nine martyrs, and that one crown remained—which had belonged to the deceased soldier—cast off his clothes, ran to the saints, and believed in Christ. When day dawned, as some appeared dead and others still breathing, they were led to the bank, their legs were broken, and finally they were placed on carts, thrown into the river, and thus completed their martyrdom.
MONTH OF THE SAME. Day Ten.
Certamen (Contest) of the holy martyrs Codratus, Cyprian, and their companions.
When the persecution was stirred up under the reign of Decius, all the Christians were either captured and slaughtered, or were hiding for a time in the mountains. At that time, the mother of Codratus, who was from the city of the Corinthians, fled, came to the mountain, and lived in the caves. And because she was pregnant, she brought forth a son, whom she named Codratus; but she did not live long afterwards, and died, leaving her son an infant. He was nourished, however, by the clouds that gathered above him and brought water, providing him with drink. As time went on, when he had reached youth, some people recognized him and came to him; among these were Cyprian, Dionysius, Anectus, Paul, and Crescens. Saint Codratus led them all and taught them the truth. After some time, having been denounced by the idolaters to the governor, they were arrested and led to Corinth; and under interrogation, as they continued to proclaim Christ to the end, they were beheaded.
And the contest of the holy martyr Dionysius.
Dionysius, Christ’s martyr, was one of those who had recognized Saint Codratus and had come to him. He was betrayed and led before the governor of the city of Corinth, because he did not obey the mandate of the emperors and despised the great gods, while preaching another God, the crucified one; saying that He is the One who made heaven and earth and the sea, and all things that are in them, and who was to come from heaven with glory to judge the living and the dead, and to render to each according to his works. Therefore, having been seized and bound, he stood before the governor,
and was urged now by blandishments, now by threats, to deny Christ and to sacrifice to idols: but adhering to his former resolve, and confessing Christ with a loud voice, he was slain by the sword, and thus completed his martyrdom.
EODEM MENSE.
Die undecima.
12 The Contest of the holy sacromartyr Pionius.
This holy man, during the reign of Decius, was a presbyter in the holy Church of Smyrna. Since he rebuked the Jews and Greeks, and demonstrated to them from the Scriptures that there is one only true God, the creator of all things, and His only-begotten Son Jesus Christ, and the Holy Spirit; and added that all sinners and infidels would be punished by Him and consigned to eternal fire, pointing out that this was evident from the Sodomite fire and that which erupts in Sicily: he was seized together with other Christians by the idolaters. First, indeed, he was bound in chains and delivered to Polemon, the priest of the idols, and to the ruler of the city of Smyrna: then he was led to the governor of the region, and by his order was subjected to most harsh scourgings, and was suspended on the rack, and his sides were scorched with torches of fire. Finally, he was taken down from the rack and cast into a burning furnace, and in prayer he completed his martyrdom.
And the memory of our holy Father Sophronius, Archbishop of Jerusalem.
Our holy Father Sophronius drew his origin from the city of Damascus in the province of Phoenicia, being the son of pious and temperate parents. Since he was endowed with an excellent intellect, he learned all the written doctrine of the Greeks and Christians. Afterward, he chose the monastery of the great Theodosius, in which he unfolded all the Scripture. Thereafter he went to Alexandria, led by the desire to acquire wider learning. Therefore, because of his doctrine and his singular virtue, he was made Bishop of Jerusalem. Then, the holy city having been captured, he went again to Alexandria to holy John the Almsgiver, and after the latter had passed from life, he returned again to Jerusalem. And since he had composed many books, and had pursued the encomia of various saints, and had written the life of holy Mary, which is beyond the powers of human nature, and had excellently led and governed the flock of the Church of God, he migrated in peace to the Lord, whom he had longed for.
EODEM MENSE.
Die duodecima.
13 Memory of our holy Father Theophanes, confessor in the Great Field.
Our holy Father Theophanes was born to noble and wealthy parents, and after his father died, he was brought up by his mother. Having reached the age of twelve, he was betrothed to a maiden, whom, by his exhortations, he induced to preserve her virginity,
and she was shorn in the monastery of Princes. As for him, having distributed his wealth to the poor, he departed and became a monk in the monastery situated on Mount Sigriana. When Leo the Armenian, an iconoclast, held the empire, learning of the virtue of Saint Theophanis, he ordered him to come to the royal city, and urged him to consent to his heresy. When he could by no means persuade him, he first ordered him to be shut up in prison. Afterwards, having brought him out of the prison and again compelling him to renounce the veneration of the venerable icons, since he saw that he would not at all tolerate hearing this, he banished him to Samothrace; where the saint went, and having lived a little while longer, he was taken up by the Lord.
And the commemoration of our holy Father Gregory, Pope of Rome.
In the reign of Justinian, this holy Gregory was a monk in a monastery near Rome; he was very virtuous, and preeminently merciful to the poor. God, wishing to test him, sent an angel to him in the guise of one shipwrecked, and found him most ready to give; for he immediately counted out fifty coins to the solicitor, then six, and finally three others, until he had exhausted the purse of gold he had in the monastery. Having become the Roman Pontiff, since he was accustomed to summon twelve poor men daily, one day there appeared to him a thirteenth, who, when asked to reveal his name, replied that this was a wonderful thing. Wherefore he was silent, understanding that he was an angel of God. Being moreover learned in all doctrines and the Scriptures, he left many works composed in the Latin tongue, which were later translated into Greek. Having lived in this way, and having performed various miracles, he departed in peace to the Lord.
ON THE SAME MONTH.
THE THIRTEENTH DAY.
The contest of the holy martyr Alexander.
Saint and glorious martyr of Christ Alexander, in the times of the persecution and amidst the darkness of the error of idolaters, shone like a very bright star with piety in the city of Pydna. When he reproved the madness of the impious, and openly preached Christ, and baptized many of the Greeks who were brought to him, he stirred up against himself the wrath of the pagans, who could barely endure his boldness and his strength in speech. Having therefore made a conspiracy, they seized him, and having subjected him to cruel examination, and having beaten him unsparingly, they urged him to sacrifice to the mindless gods. When they had accomplished nothing, they ordered him to be beheaded. And thus, giving thanks to God, he was struck on the head and delivered his blessed spirit to the Lord; but certain devout Christians collected his precious relics, and preparing them, they buried them.
And the Contest of the Holy Martyr Sabinus
Sabinus, the martyr of Christ, was from the region of Egypt. Because of the imminent severity of the persecution, he left the world, withdrew, and went outside the city, hiding himself in a small dwelling. But since a great multitude of Christians was being seized by the idol-worshippers, Sabinus too was sought; and since he was not found, he caused no little pain to the unbelievers. Then a certain beggar who was accustomed to approach Sabinus and receive from him what was necessary for his food, said to the idol-worshippers: "What will you give me, and I will show you the Sabinus whom you are seeking?" They gave him two coins, and following him, they rushed upon the dwelling, seized Sabinus, bound him, and led him to the governor. The governor then said to him: "Why, despising the edict of the emperors and the great gods, do you preach a certain unknown god?" Sabinus answered: "Because this God whom I preach is the One whom you ought to confess before all, and to believe in." And so, after tortures, he was thrown into the river and met his end.
ON THE SAME MONTH
The fourteenth day
Commemoration of our holy Father Euschemon, bishop of Lampsacus
Our holy Father and confessor of Christ, Euschemon, being well and honestly educated from an early age, became a friend of God; and as he arrived at manhood, he became a temple of the most holy Spirit, choosing the angelic life and zealously pursuing the orthodox faith. And at length, raised to the height of hierarchical honor, he was filled with spiritual grace; and being inflamed with divine zeal, he repressed and broke the heresy of the Iconoclasts. He also performed many great and wonderful miracles: among others, he brought back to life a dead infant, which had been brought to him by its weeping mother, by pouring out a prayer to God. Having become terrible to wild beasts, by his command alone he drove them from the fields where they were causing harm. Finally, having been handed over to custody by the one who then held the empire—an heretical emperor—as a worshiper of the holy icons, he persuaded his very guards themselves to become worshippers of the orthodox faith through his teaching. Wherefore, cast into exile, he met his end.
And the contest of the holy martyrs Satyrus, Saturnilus, Reucatus, Perpetua, and Felicitas, who suffered martyrdom at Rome: and also of Alexander in Pydna.
ON THE SAME MONTH
The fifteenth day
The contest of the holy martyrs Timolaus, Agapius, and those with them.
These holy and many-time-victorious martyrs of Christ lived under the emperor Diocletian. Agapius indeed was from the city of Gaza; Timolaus was from the Euxine Pontus; one Dionysius and another Dionysius were from the city of Tripoli in Phoenicia; Romulus was a subdeacon of the Church of the Diospolitans. Joining them were two Alexanders from Egypt. In the heat of the persecution, [the love] of Christ...
ignited them, and binding their own hands, they offered themselves of their own accord to the governor who at that time was torturing Christians in the city of Caesarea. And standing before him, they confessed themselves to be Christians. The governor, having exhorted them at length and compelled them to sacrifice, promising to give them gifts and honors if they obeyed, and being unable to persuade them to come over to his will, subjected them to harsh tortures; and after these tortures, he ordered their heads to be cut off with the sword: and thus they delivered their holy souls to the Lord.
Et certamen sancti martyris Nicandri. [The contest of the holy martyr Nicander.]
Nicander, martyr of Christ, flourished in the time of the emperor Diocletian. It was his constant work to visit the saints enclosed in prisons, and to minister to them and procure necessary sustenance, and also to bury their remains. Seeing, therefore, the remains of such saints so scattered and neglected, and not daring to approach them by day, lest he himself be caught, he would come by night, carry them off one after another, and deposit them in one and the same place. Having been caught, therefore, by one of the idolaters and betrayed to the governor, he was immediately seized, subjected to tortures, and compelled to deny Christ. But he refused to deny Him, and instead proclaimed Him to be the true God and Creator of all. Wherefore, having moved the governor to anger, he finished his course of life by the sword: and thus having died, he received an eternal crown and a blessed and endless life.
Et certamen sancti Apostoli Nicandri: et commemoratio sancti Joanis in Rufinianis. [And the contest of the holy Apostle Nicander: and the commemoration of the holy John in the Rufinianis.]
EODEM MENSE. [IN THE SAME MONTH.]
Die decima sexta. [The sixteenth day.]
Certamen sancti Juliani in Cilicia. [The contest of the holy Julian in Cilicia.]
Julian, martyr of Christ, was from the city of Anazarbus, the son of a certain Greek senator, having a Christian mother who taught him the holy Scriptures. When he was in his eighteenth year, he was brought by the idolaters to the city of Aegeae to the governor Marcian and compelled to sacrifice, but he refused to obey. Wherefore the executioners, violently opening his mouth, poured in wine and meat offered to idols. Then he was cast into prison, and his mother was brought in; and being questioned about him, she requested that her son be granted to her for three days, so that she might deliberate with him. This having been done, they were led back to the examination; and when they said that they would in no way deny Christ, they dismissed the mother after piercing her heels, but they cast holy Julian into a sack filled with venomous serpents and sand, and threw him into the sea: from which his remains were cast out at Alexandria and were buried by a certain devout widow.
And the commemoration of the holy apostle Aristobulus, one of the Seventy.
Aristobulus, the divine apostle of Christ, was one of the seventy disciples. After the glorious and saving ascension of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, he followed the holy apostle Paul, the great teacher of the world, into every city and region, ministering and serving him as a genuine and faithful disciple. And when that apostle was ordaining bishops and sending them into every region to teach the true faith and to preach Christ, he ordained him also and sent him into the region of the Britons, who were at that time infidel, fierce, and cruel men. As soon as he arrived among them and preached Christ, he was sometimes beaten, sometimes dragged along the ground, and repeatedly exposed to ridicule. Meanwhile, he persuaded many to come to Christ and be baptized. Whence, having established a church and ordained presbyters and deacons within it, he completed his life.
And the contest of the holy martyrs Menignus and Romanus.
The holy Menignus lived during the reign of Decius, and was from the city of Parium. He was a fuller by trade, and providing his own sustenance by the labor of his hands, he assisted the Christians who had been cast into prisons on account of the persecution. He himself also desired to suffer martyrdom for Christ, and he entreated this in his prayers. Wherefore he heard a voice saying to him: "Menignus, come to me, and you will find grace before me." He approached the judge, therefore, and confessed himself to be a Christian. On account of this, having been beaten with rods, and having had the fingers of his hands and feet cut off by the sword, he was beheaded. His venerable remains, buried in the city, provide healing to all the faithful to this present day. But Romanus, since he was a deacon of the Church of Caesarea in Palestine and was teaching the people the faith in Christ, was arrested, and after being tortured with many torments, he received his end on that same day, having been slain by the sword.
And the contest of the holy martyr Papas and the holy martyr Euphrasia: and also the commemoration of the holy Alexander, pope of Rome; and of the holy Trophimus and Thallus.
ON THE SAME MONTH. THE SEVENTEENTH DAY.
Commemoration of the holy Alexius, the man of God.
This man was from the city of Rome, the son of Euphemianus the patrician, who also compelled him to take a wife. When the marriage had been celebrated, and at the time when he ought to have consorted with his bride, he gave her his nuptial ring and departed from the house; and having set out for the city of Edessa, he remained at the church for eighteen years. Since he was recognized because of his virtue, he withdrew; and returning to Rome, he entered his own house, where, unrecognized, he stayed at the gate, looking upon his father and mother, and being treated with ridicule by his servants: while his parents, as well as his own chaste wife, were suffering and perpetually...
weeping for him. When his end was approaching, he asked for paper and wrote down everything concerning himself, and held it in his hand after his death; the emperor Honorius took it and read it for all to hear. Then his story became known. And thus his holy relic was buried in the church of the holy apostle Peter.
The Passion of the Holy Martyr Marinus
Marinus, a martyr of Christ, being a Christian and seeing the pagans sacrificing not only irrational animals, quadrupeds, and birds, but also human beings, was moved to zeal. When a festival was being held for the inanimate idols, he ran and overturned the altar, trampled the sacrifices, and heaped insults upon the impious sacrificers of the idols, confessing himself to be a Christian, saying: "I believe in Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, the maker of heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them." Then the idolaters, incensed with anger, seized him, and first they tormented him themselves: one striking him with a club, another breaking his mouth and teeth with a stone, and another pulling out his hair. Then, having bound him, they handed him over to the governor of that region; by whose order he was most miserably beaten with dry ox-tendons, and soon after suspended, his sides scorched, and finally he was beheaded with a sword.
In the Same Month, the Eighteenth Day. Commemoration of our Holy Father Cyril of Jerusalem.
He was born of pious parents during the reign of Constantius. When Maximus, the bishop of Jerusalem, reached the end of his life, this man, deemed worthy of the grace of the episcopate in his stead, took his place and zealously contended for the apostolic dogmas. But Acacius, who was an Arian and held the throne of Caesarea in Palestine, and who had been deposed by the synod of Sardica, since he was an acquaintance of the emperor, having received authority from him, cast Cyril from his seat. He departed to Tarsus and stayed with the admirable Silvanus. When the synod had been assembled at Seleucia, Acacius flew to Constantinople, and persuaded the emperor to punish Cyril with exile. After the death of Constantius, when Julian had obtained the empire and wished to render everyone well-disposed toward himself, he restored Cyril, along with the others, from exile to his own see. So, having governed his flock well, he departed to the Lord.
The Passion of the Holy Seven Women in Amisus
During the reign of the impious Maximian, when a great persecution was stirred up, people of every age who confessed Christ were cut down by different and various kinds of death. When, therefore, even in the city of Amisus, everyone who preached Christ as God was, by the governor of that same city, *an idolater,*
being put to death, seven Christian women, fervent in their zeal, stood before him and confessed themselves to be Christians. Freely reproaching him and calling him a cruel and unjust man, an enemy of the truth, they aroused his anger. Wherefore, first having been stretched out, they were beaten with rods; then their breasts were cut off with iron; soon they were suspended and lacerated for so long that their entrails appeared; finally, they were cast into a huge, fiercely burning furnace of fire, and in it, while chanting and praying, they yielded their souls to God.
ON THE SAME MONTH.
The nineteenth day.
 The contest of the holy Fathers who were killed by the Ethiopians in the monastery of Saint Saba.
These holy Fathers, gathered from diverse places and dwelling in the monastery of our holy Father Saba, served God in ascetic exercise and fair discipline. But the devil, the envious enemy of the human race, being most especially hostile to those who excel in virtue, stirred up against them the godless Ethiopians, who hoped they would find abundant wealth there. But when they had made their incursion and found nothing, they poured their rage upon them; some they slaughtered, others they cut in pieces; they severed the hands of some, and the feet of others; some they stabbed, spilling their entrails; and finally they killed others in various ways. But they, according to their custom, offering thanks and praying, yielded their blessed souls to God in this manner, receiving the eternal life of the kingdom of the heavens, for the sake of which they had endured the long struggles of the ascetic life and the martyrdom of laborious contest.
ON THE SAME MONTH.
The twentieth day.
The contest of the holy Photina the Samaritan, and of her companions.
Saint Photina, who was also the Samaritan woman with whom the Lord spoke at the well, lived in the time of Nero. After the passing of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, she dwelt with her son Joseph in the city of Carthage in Africa, preaching Christ. Her son Victor, having performed well against the Avars, was made a leader of armies, and was ordered to kill the Christians of Galilee. But when he did not kill them, but rather taught them all things pertaining to Christ, and had persuaded Sebastian to believe in Christ, he was seized and bound, and brought together with the others, and presented to the emperor. The emperor gouged out the eyes of some, cast others into prison, and suspended others on wood; from some he flayed the skin, and cut off the virile parts of others. He bound Photina to two trees bent with great force, and releasing them, he rent her in two. The rest were beheaded. But Photina ended her life in prison.
And the commemoration of our holy Father Thomas, Patriarch of Constantinople.
Our holy Father Thomas, on account of his surpassing virtue, his extreme prudence, and his piety, was ordained deacon of the Great Church and sacellarius by our holy Father and most great worker of miracles, John, surnamed the Faster, during the reign of the praiseworthy and blessed Maurice. After the death of this John and of Cyriacus, who succeeded him in the episcopate, he was ordained Patriarch of Constantinople, and he held that episcopate for three years and two months. Having contended much against the heresies and having put the heretics themselves to shame, and having established the orthodox doctrine, and having shepherded his flock well and to the good pleasure of God, and having instructed the pious emperors excellently, and having appeared venerable to the senate and to the entire priestly order, he was seized by illness, and he flew away to the heavens, rejoicing and exulting, as was fitting.
ON THE SAME DAY.
The twenty-first.
Commemoration of our holy Father Benedict, archimandrite of Rome.
This man came from the city of Rome, and was called Blessed. While still a boy, he left his home and parents and went out into a desert place with his nurse, an elderly woman, and lived a quiet life; and through prayer he received from God the gifts of healing. For when he was first made abbot at the request of the monks, he soon became hated by them on account of his strict abstinence, and he was plotted against with poisonous drink. Yet when he received the cup and made the sign of the cross over it, the glass dissolved like salt. Later, he performed many other miracles as well. When he was about to depart to the Lord, two pious monks appeared to him in a dream, seeing a path extending from the earth to heaven, spread with precious robes and shining with lamps lit on either side. And when they asked whose path this was, a man adorned in white raiment appeared to have answered: "This is the way of Benedict." And in this manner he finished his life and went to heaven.
And the commemoration of our holy Father James the Younger, who was a bishop.
James, the holy one, chose the ascetic life from his tenderest years; and having become a monk, he first purified himself through fasting, vigils, and other hardships, and especially through the meditation of the sacred Scriptures and steady prayers to God. Later, he was deemed worthy of the episcopal dignity. But during the times of the impious Iconoclasts, being greatly provoked by them to renounce the worship of the holy and venerable icons—and since he refused to do so—he endured many temptations; he underwent unbearable exiles, hunger, thirst, and many other things which the impious devised against him, and he stood firm. Finally, throughout these many tortures...
worn by various torments and afflictions, he surrendered his blessed soul into the hands of God; and because he had fought generously even unto death, he attained the heavenly kingdom and exults with Him forever.
Et commemoratio sancti Berylli episcopi Catanæ.
The Commemoration of Saint Beryllus, Bishop of Catana.
Our holy Father Beryllus was of Syrian Antioch, having become a disciple of the holy apostle Peter, by whom he was ordained Bishop of Catana in Sicily. Having shepherded the flock excellently and led them into the pastures of salvation, and having brought many of the infidels to the faith of Christ, he was rendered worthy of the gift of many miracles; of which it is necessary to mention one here. There was a fountain near that place containing very bitter water, which, by pouring out prayers to God, he transformed into sweet drink. When a certain Greek, most fanatically addicted to idolatry, saw this, he believed in Christ, and with him many others. When he had performed other not infrequent miracles, and had reached a deep old age, he migrated to the Lord, having obtained eternal life from Him. But his venerable relics, honorably interred in that island, confer health even to this day upon all who approach them with faith.
EODEM MENSE. Die vicesima secunda
Of the Same Month. The Twenty-Second Day.
Commemoratio sancti Artemonis episcopi Seleuciæ.
The Commemoration of Saint Artemon, Bishop of Seleucia.
The blessed Artemon had Seleucia as his fatherland and city, seeing that he was born and educated in it. When, however, the blessed Paul came there, he became his disciple; and afterwards, he was the bishop of the same city of Seleucia, a teacher of the people, and a herald of the truth. Wherefore, having performed many miracles, he converted not a few from among the idolaters from their error to the Lord, and made them Christians through divine, most august, and saving baptism. After these things, piously and as it was pleasing to God, directing the flock entrusted to him and governing the Church, he became a harbor of salvation for all who were in need, a defender of widows, a protector of orphans, and a guide of beggars and the poor. Exercising himself in these works, and serving God in all things, he migrated to Him with joy in deep old age, having obtained eternal life.

### Et certamen sacrosancti martyris Basilii presbyteri Ancyranorum Ecclesiæ. — The Contest of the Holy Martyr Basil, Priest of the Church of Ancyra
And the Contest of the Most Holy Martyr Basil, Presbyter of the Church of Ancyra.
EODEM MENSE. Die vicesima tertia
Of the Same Month. The Twenty-Third Day.
The contest of the sacrosanct martyr Nicon, and of one hundred and ninety-nine companion martyrs.
The Contest of the Most Holy Martyr Nicon and his one hundred and ninety-nine companion martyrs.
This man lived in the times of the prefect Quintianus, born in the region of Neapolis, of a Christian mother, but of a Greek father. When he was serving as a soldier, and a dangerous struggle was imminent, he groaned heavily,
and saying, "Lord Jesus Christ, God of my mother, help me," he performed feats worthy of a brave man. A Afterwards, having returned and informed his mother of his purpose, and being instructed by an angel appearing to him, he departed for Mount Ganus. Having found a bishop there in a cave, he was baptized by him, and remained there for ten years, and was ordained bishop by him. Thereafter, the bishop also entrusted to him one hundred and ninety-nine monks; and thus his life was completed. But knowing by revelation that the mountain was about to be destroyed by the Gentiles, he took the monks and departed for Mitylene, then for Italy. Where his mother, having found him, and embraced him, immediately died. Having left for Mount Tauromenium, he lived there with his disciples. And the governor, sending and laying hold of them, beheaded them.
The Contest of the Holy Martyr Dometius.
Dometius, the martyr of Christ, was indeed during the tyranny of Julian the Apostate, from the region of Phrygia. But seeing many who were attached to the tyrant, and daily renouncing Christ and worshipping idols, he was deeply troubled, and anxious in spirit, and saddened with great grief. Therefore, on a certain day, when horse races were being held and sacrifices being offered to the unclean demons, he could not contain himself, but inflamed with divine zeal, he went into the middle of the theater, and with a loud voice anathematized the apostate Julian, and spat upon the idol-worshippers, and mocked the falsely-named gods. Having been seized, therefore, and bound securely, he was delivered to the governor, and having endured many tortures, he was shut up in prison. And after a few days he was brought out of the prison, and compelled to deny Christ, and as he did not consent, his sacred head was cut off with a sword.
ON THE SAME MONTH. The twenty-fourth day.
The Contest of the Holy Thirty-Five Martyrs of Caesarea.
These holy thirty-five martyrs of Christ also flourished in Caesarea of Palestine: who after the decree was sent forth by the impious and lawless Julian, ordering Christ to be denied, and the gods of the Greeks to be worshipped, were not only not persuaded to do this, but also having assumed noble boldness, and going about through the whole city, they said with a loud voice: "Let Christ alone, as the true God, be honored and worshipped; but let the gods who did not make heaven and earth perish with all who worship them." Having been seized, therefore, by the idol-worshippers, they were delivered to prison, and having been brought before the apostate from Christ, Julian, by the lawless order of that man their heads were eagerly cut off, and they flew up to Christ, whom they had desired from infancy and had never denied; and thus they obtained the reward of immortality.
OF THE SAME MONTH. The Twenty-Fifth Day
25. The Annunciation of the most holy Theotokos.
Our lover of mankind and merciful God, who always keeps a solicitous care for the human race, when He beheld man, the handiwork of His hands, being enslaved by the devil, willed to send His only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, to rescue him from the devil’s hands. But since He willed it to be unknown not only to Satan, but even to the heavenly powers themselves, He entrusted this mystery to one of the archangels, the glorious Gabriel. He provided in His providence that the holy Virgin be born, pure and immaculate, being worthy of such a great good. Therefore, Gabriel came into the city called Nazareth and said to her: "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee." She truly said: "How shall this be to me?" To whom he said: "The Holy Spirit," he says, "shall come upon thee, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow thee." Then she: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord, be it done to me according to thy word." With this said, she conceived the Son and Word of God in a supernatural manner: and then all the mysteries of the Word of God were fulfilled, as is befitting for man, for our salvation.
OF THE SAME MONTH. The Twenty-Sixth Day
The contest of the saints who suffered martyrdom in Gothia.
These were under Vingurichus, prince of the Goths, when Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian were Roman emperors. When all were chanting in the church of the Christians and singing praises to God, Vingurichus, sending soldiers, set the church on fire and burned them all together.
